items.title: 18.7.1 Ligand Exchange Reactions of Copper(II) Complexes

source_refs.note: Topic 18.7.1 (PDF 28); Figures 18.7 and 18.8 are replaced by an original diagram, and the precipitate-dissolving equation is taken from Quick Check 18.5.

blocks.text: Cu2+(aq) actually means the complex ion [Cu(H2O)6]2+, which gives copper(II) salt solutions, such as copper sulphate solution, their blue colour.

blocks.caption: Ligand exchange reactions of copper(II)
rows: blue solution gives a light blue precipitate; two OH- replace two H2O
excess conc. NH3 on the precipitate
precipitate dissolves to a dark blue solution
blue to dark blue; four NH3 replace four H2O

blocks.alt: [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ in square brackets: Cu in the centre with four NH3 at the corners of a dashed square plane (the front two on wedge bonds, the back two on dashed bonds) and one H2O above and one below the plane.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.7: Structure of [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+(aq) ion (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.7).

blocks.alt: Three flasks. Middle ('Start here'): blue [Cu(H2O)6]2+, the well-known blue Cu2+ complex with water. Left, beside a conc. HCl bottle: yellow-green [CuCl4]2-, which forms on adding conc. HCl. Right, beside a conc. NH3 bottle: dark blue [Cu(H2O)2(NH3)4]2+, which forms on adding conc. NH3. Equilibrium arrows join the flasks.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.8: Colour changes as a result of ligand exchange reaction (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.8).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption text reads 'This is yellow-green complex forms...'; it should read 'This yellow-green complex forms...'.
